# Best portable power station for a CPAP

For most people, I'd pick the **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (1,024 Wh, about $700). Which unit is best depends on your humidifier use and budget, so there are alternatives below.

## Top picks

| Pick | Why | Price | Nights (humidifier off / on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (best overall) | Quietest rating (~20 dB under 200 W), 10 ms UPS switchover, ~49 min recharge, 24.9 lb | ~$700 | ~2.7 / ~1.2-1.7 |
| **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (best if you want to expand) | Same capacity, can expand up to 5 kWh, up to 1,000 W solar input | ~$719 | ~2.7 / ~1.2-1.7 |
| **Bluetti Elite 100 V2** (best value) | 1,024 Wh at a lower price | ~$499 | ~2.7 / ~1.2 |
| **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** (small, light) | 10.4 lb, under 10 ms UPS, expandable | ~$299 | ~0.8 / ~0.3-0.5 |

Sources: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) for the Anker, DELTA 3 Plus and RIVER 3 Plus specs, [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) for prices and runtimes, and [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap) for the Bluetti Elite 100 V2.

## Things to know

- **Humidifier use decides the size.** A heated humidifier roughly doubles power draw. A ~1,000 Wh unit gives about 2.7 dry nights but only about 1.2-1.7 humidified nights. Sources use different assumptions (320-720 Wh per humidified night), so treat these as estimates.
- **Size it yourself.** The formula is nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For two humidified nights at 520 Wh, you need about 1,220 Wh. A 2,000 Wh unit like the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 ($899, ~2.4 humidified nights) fits that case.
- **Only pure sine wave.** All the units above qualify, but confirm it on any other model you consider.
- **UPS switchover** (about 10 ms or faster) keeps therapy running if the grid drops while you sleep. The Anker and EcoFlow units meet this.
- **Use your CPAP's DC cord** with the 12 V port if you want to stretch runtime by roughly 10-20%. Use only the cord your CPAP maker approves.

## Cautions

- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** ($499, 1,070 Wh) is cheap and light, but Tested Watts notes that Jackery says its stations are [not recommended for medical devices](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/). Its UPS switchover is also slower, at up to 20 ms. I'd skip it unless your CPAP maker confirms it's fine.
- **RIVER 3 Plus** is described as "multi-night" by [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/). That conflicts with the other sources (under one night, even humidifier-off), and the math (286 Wh ÷ ~40 W) supports them. Only buy it with an expansion battery or if your CPAP draws very little.
- The Tested Watts and PowerStationBench pages say they research specs rather than lab-test units. Check your machine's wattage label and ask your provider or CPAP supplier about a backup plan.

## Where to buy

I don't have direct product links from these results. The [BuyerSheet comparison table](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) has "Check on Amazon" and "Check official store" buttons for each model above. [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap) has Amazon links for the Bluetti Elite 100 V2 and Elite 200 V2. Prices change often, so confirm before you buy.

If you tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the humidifier, I can narrow this to one pick.
